problems.title: Shortest distance from a line to a circle
problems.question: M lies on 3x+4y+34=0 and N on x²+y²−8x+2y−8=0. Find the minimum MN.
problems.idea: Subtract the radius from the centre-to-line distance.
steps: The centre is (4,−1), radius 5. Its distance to the line is 42/5.
Because the line is outside the circle, the minimum gap is 42/5−5=17/5.

problems.title: A probability in the unit square
problems.question: Choose x,y independently and uniformly from [0,1]. Find P(x≤2y and y≤3x).
problems.idea: The two forbidden triangles are disjoint except at the origin.
steps: The region x>2y has area 1/4. The region y>3x has area 1/6.

problems.title: Arithmetic progression imposes a quadratic
problems.question: The numbers x/2,(x²+3)/2,(5x+2)/2 form an arithmetic progression. Find the sum of the squares of all possible x.
problems.idea: Twice the middle term equals the sum of its neighbours.
steps: This simplifies to x²−3x+2=0, so x=1 or 2.

problems.title: A nonincreasing geometric progression
problems.question: The first two terms sum to −1 and the next two sum to −4. Find the sum of the first six terms of the nonincreasing geometric progression.
problems.idea: The second pair sum is q² times the first pair sum.
steps: q=−2 alternates signs and cannot be nonincreasing. Thus q=2 and a=−1/3.

problems.title: A root-square condition with an endpoint issue
problems.question: For which q does x²−6x+q=0 have two real roots whose squared sum is less than 26?
problems.idea: Use the sum and product of roots and check the discriminant.
steps: The squared-sum condition gives q>5. Reality gives q≤9.
At q=9 the repeated roots are 3 and 3, with squared sum 18, which satisfies the bound.
If two distinct roots are intended, use q<9 instead.
problems.answer: 5<q≤9 counting a double root; 5<q<9 for distinct roots.
problems.note: The printed choice (5,9) assumes distinct roots, which the wording should state explicitly.

problems.title: Two different positive quadratic roots
problems.question: Find a such that x²−x+a=0 has two distinct positive roots.
problems.idea: Require a positive product, positive sum and positive discriminant.
steps: The positive sum rules out two negative roots; the positive product ensures the roots have the same sign.

problems.title: Recover a convergent geometric ratio
problems.question: An infinite convergent geometric progression has sum 3 and second term 3/4. Find its ratio.
problems.idea: Express its first term using the sum.

problems.title: Standard deviation of four data values
problems.question: Find the population standard deviation of 0,0,1,3.
problems.idea: Find the mean and then the mean squared deviation.
steps: The mean is 1. The squared deviations are 1,1,0,4.
Their average is 6/4=3/2. Take its square root.

problems.title: A median and angle bisector in a right triangle
problems.question: A right triangle has legs 6 and 3. From the right-angle vertex C draw median CM and bisector CK to the hypotenuse. Find area CMK.
problems.idea: Use MK as the base and the altitude from C to the hypotenuse as the height.
formulas: Hypotenuse=3√5; the bisector divides it 2:1; altitude=6·3/(3√5).
steps: The midpoint and the 2:1 division point are separated by one sixth of the hypotenuse, so MK=√5/2.

problems.title: The smallest natural-valued term
problems.question: Find the smallest natural-number term of xₙ=(n²−n−19)/(n−1), for positive integer indices where defined.
problems.idea: Divide the numerator by n−1.
steps: For xₙ to be an integer, n−1 must divide 19. Thus n−1=1 or 19.
The corresponding terms are x₂=−17 and x₂₀=19.

problems.title: Conditional uniform probability on an interval
problems.question: A number is chosen uniformly from the solution set x²≤16. Find the probability that it also satisfies x²+2x>15.
problems.idea: Find the two solution sets and compare lengths.
steps: The second inequality gives x<−5 or x>3. Its intersection with [−4,4] is (3,4].
The favourable length is 1 and the total length 8.

problems.title: Collinear vectors and their difference
problems.question: Two collinear vectors have dot product 4 and the sum of their lengths is 5. Find the square of the length of their difference.
problems.idea: A positive dot product means the collinear vectors point the same way.

problems.title: Resolve two vectors into components
problems.question: Vector a lies along the x-axis with length 4. Vector b has positive components, length 3, and makes angle 60° with a. Find a−b.
problems.idea: Positive b-components and an acute angle require a to point in the positive x direction.

problems.title: Count positive sequence terms
problems.question: How many positive terms does xₙ=(134−n²)/(3n−1) have for positive integer n?
problems.idea: The denominator is positive at every allowed index.

problems.title: A fourth-root substitution
problems.question: Simplify $\left(\frac{a+\sqrt[4]{ab^3}}{\sqrt a+\sqrt[4]{ab}}-\sqrt[4]{ab}\right):(\sqrt[4]a-\sqrt[4]b)^2$ for a=199,b=2018.
problems.idea: Put u=⁴√a and v=⁴√b.
steps: Since a≠b, division by (u−v)² is valid and gives 1.

problems.title: An angle-bisector point from coordinates
problems.question: In triangle A(5,5),B(2,1),C(−1,−3), AK is an angle bisector. Find K.
problems.idea: First check whether the stated points form a triangle.
steps: A,B,C are collinear, so there is no nondegenerate triangle or ordinary interior angle bisector.
If the intended exercise is merely the formal ratio BK:KC=AB:AC=1:2, the section point is (2B+C)/3=(1,−1/3).
problems.answer: No valid triangle as printed; formal section point (1,−1/3).
problems.note: The listed answer (1,−1/3) comes from the section formula, but the three supplied vertices are collinear.

problems.title: The triangle inequality for two distances
problems.question: Find the minimum of $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}+\sqrt{(a-1)^2+(b+3)^2}$.
problems.idea: The expression is a sum of distances from a point to two fixed points.
steps: Let P=(a,b). The two radicals are OP and PQ.
Equality is attained whenever P lies on the segment OQ.

problems.title: A trapezoid vertex as a vector combination
problems.question: In trapezoid ABCD, AD=k·BC as lengths, with the bases directed the same way from A to D and B to C. Given QA=a,QB=b,QC=c, express QD.
problems.idea: The directed base vectors satisfy AD=kBC.

problems.title: Two names among a class of 25
problems.question: A class has 25 pupils, including three named Anna and two named Luka. Two pupils are chosen together. Find the probability of choosing one Anna and one Luka.
problems.idea: Count unordered pairs.
steps: Divide 6 by 300. No order factor is needed because both counts use unordered pairs.

problems.title: Two square carpets in opposite corners
problems.question: Two square carpets occupy opposite corners of a square room. Their overlap has perimeter 40; one uncovered rectangle has perimeter 60. Find the room’s area.
problems.idea: Let room side be L and carpet sides u,v.
steps: The uncovered rectangle perimeter gives 2[(L−u)+(L−v)]=60, hence 2L−u−v=30.
Add the equations to obtain L=40.

problems.title: Compare two regular polygons in the same circle
problems.question: Find the area ratio of a regular dodecagon to a regular octagon inscribed in the same circle.
problems.idea: Split each into congruent triangles from the centre.

problems.title: The angle between a vector and a sum
problems.question: |a|=1, |b|=2 and the angle between them is 60°. Find cos of the angle between a and a+b.
problems.idea: Use a dot product and the length of the sum.

problems.title: A crescent between two circles
problems.question: A common chord AB has length 6. It is a side of a regular hexagon inscribed in one circle and of an equilateral triangle inscribed in the other. Find the shaded crescent shown.
problems.idea: Subtract the larger circle’s small segment from the smaller circle’s small segment.
steps: The large radius is 6 and its chord angle is 60°. Its small segment has area 6π−9√3.
The small radius is 2√3 and its chord angle is 120°. Its small segment has area 4π−3√3.

problems.title: A dice sum bounded above
problems.question: A die is rolled twice. Find the probability that the sum is at most 10.
problems.idea: Use the complement.

problems.title: An entering person changes an average
problems.question: Three people in a room have average age 11. A fourth enters and the average becomes 14. Find the new person’s age.
problems.idea: Compare total ages before and after.
steps: The original total is 33. The new total is 56.
